exposure: Neonatal clinical features (Lethargy, low nutrition, vomit, hypothermia, intubation)
Bacterial etiology (Staphylococcus aureus, Coagulase-negative staphylococci, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumonia)
Antibiotic resistance profile (e.g., to penicillin, ampicillin)
outcome: Antibiotic susceptibility profile of isolated bacteria
cohort: A cohort of 592 newborns, admitted with their mothers to two gynecological and maternity hospitals in Shiraz, Iran, for suspected neonatal sepsis.
finding: Both neonatal and maternal factors, including maternal age, gestational age, and mode of delivery, were significantly associated with neonatal sepsis, with *Staphylococcus aureus* and Coagulase-negative staphylococci being the predominant and often resistant bacterial species.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as a maternal characteristic significantly associated with neonatal sepsis.
cross-section timing: During admission to gynecological and maternity hospitals for suspected neonatal sepsis.
gest_age: Gestational age was measured and found to be significantly associated with neonatal sepsis.
